name: Evernote
tagline: Long-running note app for capture, search, tasks, and cross-device notes

pricing.notes: Official Evernote plan pages checked 2026-07-30; current plan names have changed, and Starter is listed around $14.99/month in public plan references.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 50 notes; 1 notebook; 5 spaces; 20 tags; 1 device; 1 GB storage; 200 attachments; 1 calendar; 250 MB uploads/month; 200 MB max note/attachment

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 1,000 notes; 20 notebooks; 1,000 attachments; 10 spaces; 100 tags; 3 devices; 5 GB storage; 5 calendars

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.limits: Unlimited notes, notebooks, devices, attachments and storage under safeguards; 12,000 spaces; 100,000 tags; 5 calendars

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom organization controls and support; 500 GB shared monthly upload allowance; monthly or annual contract

pricing.freeTierCaps: 50 notes, 1 notebook, 5 spaces, 20 tags, 1 device, 1 GB storage, 200 attachments, 1 calendar, 250 MB uploads/month and 200 MB max note/attachment
pricing.billingTerms: Starter/Advanced monthly + annual; Enterprise monthly or annual quote; third-party app-store prices may differ
pricing.hiddenCosts: Advanced's 'unlimited' limits retain anti-abuse safeguards. Apple/Google prices may differ from direct billing. Exceeding Starter caps can force content reduction or an upgrade.

verdictSummary: A personal notes app with OCR/search/import is reachable, but the hard parts are migration, sync reliability, clipper UX, OCR quality, and years of user data.
coreLoopDIY: Create a Markdown/database notes app with tags, attachments, web clipper, OCR pass, and full-text search.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because all old notes, attachments, scans, and clipped pages are already there.

priorArt.name: Joplin
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source note app with sync, markdown notes, clipping, and end-to-end encryption

alternatives.name: Joplin
alternatives.desc: Evernote after removing the rent, the lock-in and some polish.

facts.install: Official desktop, mobile, or terminal package; optional Joplin Server via Docker
facts.dataFormat: The app keeps notes and metadata in its local profile database, with Markdown bodies and resource attachments; JEX/raw exports are available, and optional sync copies encrypted items to Joplin Cloud, Dropbox, OneDrive, WebDAV, S3, or Joplin Server
facts.gapVsPaid: Joplin is less polished at document scanning, OCR, web clipping, email capture, and search across messy attachments than Evernote.
facts.setupBlocker: Local use installs cleanly; dependable multi-device use means choosing and configuring a sync target, then correctly enabling and preserving end-to-end-encryption keys

alternatives.name: Notesnook
alternatives.desc: Evernote with the server blindfolded and the free tier still usable.

facts.install: Hosted web/desktop/mobile app, or an experimental Docker self-hosted sync stack
facts.dataFormat: Notes are encrypted on the device and the hosted or self-hosted sync service stores encrypted per-item data; local app data remains on-device and encrypted .nnbackupz backups can be exported
facts.gapVsPaid: Notesnook prioritizes encrypted notes but has a less mature task, calendar, scanning, web-clipping, and integration ecosystem than Evernote.
facts.setupBlocker: Hosted use installs cleanly; self-hosting is explicitly experimental and requires Docker plus MongoDB, MinIO/S3-compatible storage, secrets, backups, and client endpoint configuration

alternatives.name: SiYuan
alternatives.desc: Capture, search, tasks and databases; free sync means bringing your own server.

facts.install: Desktop/mobile package, or Docker image for browser-based self-hosting
facts.engines: Built-in AI features connect to OpenAI-compatible APIs using a configured endpoint and key
facts.dataFormat: A workspace stores block documents as structured .sy JSON files plus assets on disk; SQLite files hold indexes and auxiliary state; documents can export to Markdown, HTML, PDF, and Word
facts.gapVsPaid: SiYuan is stronger at structured knowledge than frictionless capture, and its mobile scanning, web clipping, OCR, and turnkey sync are weaker than Evernote's.
facts.setupBlocker: The desktop app installs cleanly, but free cross-device sync is not a turnkey feature: official cloud sync is a paid membership feature and Docker hosting does not transparently become desktop/mobile sync

notes: A good example where core notes are easy but switching costs and capture depth drive retention.
prompt:
Build me a personal capture-and-notes app to replace Evernote. Requirements:

- A local web app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3, server-rendered pages,
  binds to localhost.
- Notes are Markdown stored in SQLite with tags, edited in a textarea with live
  preview via marked.
- Attachments: drag a file or image onto a note, stored in ./data/files/ and
  linked from the note. On upload, run tesseract.js OCR over images and PDF
  pages and store the extracted text so scans and receipts are searchable.
- Full-text search across notes plus OCR text with SQLite FTS5, search box in
  the header, tag filters beside it.
- Capture via bookmarklet: POSTs the current page's title, URL, and selected
  text into a new note. A bookmarklet, not an extension.
- An import script for Evernote .enex exports: notes, tags, and attachments,
  so my old data actually moves in.
- Weekly export of everything to a folder of .md files plus attachments, so
  nothing is ever trapped in the app.
- No accounts, no telemetry, all data on my machine.
- Out of scope: mobile apps, cross-device sync, a real browser extension.
- README: setup steps and where the data lives on disk.
